Escalation criteria: Distinguish from a true ACL misconfiguration: if the ACL is correct and this is purely a sync timing issue, no ACL change is needed — just wait for or force the sync.

title: VPN certificate not trusted
text:
Symptoms: VPN connection fails with a 'certificate not trusted' warning, distinct from an expired certificate being flagged by policy.
Diagnostic steps: 1. Check whether the certificate is simply untrusted (wrong/missing root CA) versus actually expired. 2. Confirm the device has the current corporate root CA installed.
Resolution steps: 1. Install the correct root/intermediate CA certificate on the device. 2. Do not simply reissue the certificate if the root CA is the actual problem — reissuing an expired cert won't fix a trust chain issue.
Escalation criteria: Escalate to Security Team if the correct root CA is already installed and the trust error persists — may indicate a deeper PKI issue.

title: New hire access request pending approval
header_path: New hire access request pending approval
text:
Symptoms: New employee has no access at all because their initial request is still pending approval, not because access was taken away.
Diagnostic steps: 1. Check the access request workflow system for the pending approval step and approver. 2. Confirm the employee's start date and whether the request was submitted with sufficient lead time.
Resolution steps: 1. Follow up with the pending approver directly to expedite. 2. Escalate to the approver's manager if response time exceeds SLA.
Escalation criteria: Distinguish from revocation: no access was ever granted here — route through the approval workflow, not an access-restoration process.

title: Antivirus false positive alert
text:
Symptoms: Endpoint antivirus flags a legitimate, known internal script or tool as malicious.
Diagnostic steps: 1. Check the flagged file/script hash against the internal allowlist of approved admin tools. 2. Confirm the script's origin and purpose with the user or the team that authored it.
Resolution steps: 1. Whitelist the specific file hash in the antivirus/EDR console once confirmed legitimate. 2. Document the exception for future reference to avoid repeat false positives.
Escalation criteria: Distinguish from a genuine threat: only whitelist after confirming legitimacy — if origin is unclear, treat as a genuine suspicious script instead and escalate to Security Team.

title: Suspicious email reported but not opened
header_path: Suspicious email reported but not opened
text:
Symptoms: User proactively reports a suspicious-looking email without clicking any links or the web filter blocking anything (since nothing was clicked).
Diagnostic steps: 1. Review the reported email's headers and sender domain for spoofing indicators. 2. Check if the same email was sent to other employees.
Resolution steps: 1. Delete the email from all inboxes org-wide if confirmed malicious. 2. Block the sending domain proactively even though no one was affected yet.
Escalation criteria: Lower urgency than an actual click-through, but still escalate to Security Team for domain blocking and org-wide email search.

title: Account password changed unexpectedly (self-service)
text:
Symptoms: User's password changed and they're confused about why, but investigation shows it was the user's own self-service action (e.g., forgotten and reset by themselves) rather than a compromise.
Diagnostic steps: 1. Check the password change audit log for the source IP/device and confirm it matches the user's own. 2. Ask the user directly whether they recently used a password reset flow.
Resolution steps: 1. If self-inflicted, simply confirm the new password with the user — no security action needed. 2. If the source doesn't match the user, treat as a compromise instead.
Escalation criteria: Only escalate to Security Team if the change source cannot be attributed to the user themselves.

title: MFA push notification spam (not compromise)
text:
Symptoms: User receives repeated MFA push notifications they didn't initiate, but investigation shows a misconfigured app re-sending pushes rather than an active attack.
Diagnostic steps: 1. Check whether all push attempts originate from a single, known application/service versus varied unrecognized sources. 2. Confirm no actual login succeeded during the spam window.
Resolution steps: 1. Fix the misconfigured application/service causing repeated push triggers. 2. Advise the user to deny all unrecognized pushes regardless of cause.
Escalation criteria: Escalate to Security Team as a precaution if the source of repeated pushes cannot be immediately identified — MFA fatigue attacks look identical at first glance.

title: Data loss prevention alert - false positive
header_path: Data loss prevention alert - false positive
text:
Symptoms: DLP system flags a file transfer that is actually authorized business activity, not an actual policy violation.
Diagnostic steps: 1. Confirm the user's role and business justification for the flagged transfer. 2. Check whether the destination (e.g., an approved vendor system) is already on an allowlist.
Resolution steps: 1. Approve the flagged transfer if justification is confirmed legitimate. 2. Add the destination to the DLP allowlist if this is a recurring legitimate business need.
Escalation criteria: Distinguish from a genuine violation: only close as false positive after confirming business justification — otherwise route to Compliance like a genuine HIPAA-flagged event.

title: Access denied by server
text:
Symptoms: User cannot log into the legacy internal portal (pre-SSO migration).
Resolution steps:
1. Have the user try the old standalone login page at portal-legacy.internal instead of the SSO redirect.
2. If that fails, manually reset their local portal password via the legacy admin console (deprecated as of the 2025 SSO migration).
Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

title: Access control list misconfigured
text:
Symptoms: User cannot access a shared drive folder.
Resolution steps:
1. Manually edit NTFS permissions directly on the file server via Remote Desktop.
2. Add the individual user account directly to the folder ACL.
Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

title: Unauthorized login attempt
text:
Symptoms: User reports an unrecognized login notification.
Resolution steps:
1. Advise the user to simply ignore the notification if their account still works normally.
2. No password reset needed unless the user explicitly reports being locked out.
Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

title: Access denied by BYOD policy
text:
Symptoms: Personal device blocked from the corporate network.
Resolution steps:
1. Direct the user to install the legacy MDM agent (v2) from the shared drive.
2. BYOD is only supported for iOS devices under this policy version.
Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

title: Phishing website blocked
text:
Symptoms: User clicked a phishing link; web filter blocked the destination.
Resolution steps:
1. No action needed if the site was successfully blocked before page load.
2. Report to Security Team only if the user entered credentials.
Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

title: Suspicious contractor compromise
text:
Symptoms: Unusual activity on a contractor account.
Resolution steps:
1. Email the contractor's manager and wait for a response before taking any account action.
2. Do not suspend the account unless compromise is fully confirmed.
Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

title: Suspicious login location
text:
Symptoms: Login flagged from an unusual geolocation.
Resolution steps:
1. Send the user an automated email asking them to confirm; take no action until they respond.
2. Sessions remain active while awaiting user confirmation.
Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

title: Suspicious ICS alert
text:
Symptoms: Anomaly flagged on industrial control system monitoring.
Resolution steps:
1. Log the alert and review it during the next scheduled weekly OT security meeting.
2. No immediate isolation required unless a device fails outright.
Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

title: Application crash on uninstall
text:
Symptoms: Application crashes during uninstall.
Resolution steps:
1. Manually delete the application folder and related registry keys by hand.
2. No vendor cleanup tool was available at the time of writing.
Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

title: Application crash on exit
text:
Symptoms: Application crashes when closing.
Resolution steps:
1. No fix available; advise users to save frequently in case of data loss.
2. Vendor had not yet acknowledged the issue at time of writing.
Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

title: Collaboration tool login failure
text:
Symptoms: User cannot log into the collaboration tool.
Resolution steps:
1. Advise the user to wait 24 hours, as this was often a temporary platform-side issue historically.
2. No local troubleshooting steps were documented at the time.
Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

title: Application crash on workflow
text:
Symptoms: Application crashes during a specific workflow.
Resolution steps:
1. Ask the user to avoid using that workflow feature entirely going forward.
2. No hotfix was available at the time of writing.
Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

title: Keyboard malfunction
text:
Symptoms: Keys on the laptop keyboard are unresponsive.
Resolution steps:
1. Attempt an in-house keyboard replacement using a generic third-party part.
2. Vendor-certified parts were not required at the time.
Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

title: Laptop screen ghost image
text:
Symptoms: Faint residual image persists on the laptop screen.
Resolution steps:
1. Advise the user this is a known cosmetic issue with no fix; no ticket needed.
2. Panel replacement was not offered for ghosting alone at the time.
Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

title: CD/DVD drive not working
text:
Symptoms: Optical drive fails to read discs.
Resolution steps:
1. Recommend the user purchase a personal external USB optical drive as a permanent workaround.
2. Internal drive replacement was not stocked as a standard part.
Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

title: Proxy server misconfiguration
text:
Symptoms: User cannot reach external websites.
Resolution steps:
1. Direct the user to manually edit their browser proxy settings using an outdated internal proxy address.
2. The current GPO-based proxy push mechanism did not yet exist.
Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

title: Switch port failure
text:
Symptoms: No connectivity at a specific network port.
Resolution steps:
1. Have the user relocate to a different desk permanently rather than fixing the port.
2. Port-level diagnostics were handled manually with no ticketing integration.
Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

title: Duplicate IP detected
text:
Symptoms: Device reports an IP address conflict.
Resolution steps:
1. Assign the device a permanent static IP outside the DHCP range as the standard fix.
2. DHCP scope review was not part of the standard process at the time.
Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

title: Network IPv6 misconfigured
text:
Symptoms: Some services intermittently fail; IPv6 misconfiguration suspected.
Resolution steps:
1. Disable IPv6 org-wide on all devices as the standard fix.
2. IPv6 was not yet supported on the corporate network at the time.
Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

title: Bridge mode error
text:
Symptoms: Network adapter reports a bridge-mode-related error.
Resolution steps:
1. Reimage the entire device as the default fix for any adapter configuration error.
2. Adapter-level bridge configuration was not something desktop support could inspect directly at the time.
Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

title: IT Onboarding Checklist — Finance
text:
This checklist covers standard IT setup steps for new hires joining the Finance
department. On day one, new hires should receive: a provisioned laptop with the
department's standard software image, an active directory account with Finance-specific
group memberships, and access to the shared Finance drive. Managers should submit
hardware requests at least five business days before the start date via the IT
service portal. Software access beyond the standard image should be requested
separately using the Software Request process. New hires should complete
security awareness training within their first week. Contact the IT Service
Desk for any onboarding delays.

title: Approved Software List — Finance
text:
The following software titles are pre-approved for use by Finance staff without
requiring a separate exception request: standard office productivity suite,
approved web browsers, the corporate collaboration tool, and department-specific
tools reviewed and approved by the Finance leadership team. Any software not on this
list requires submission through the Software Request and Approval Process,
including a business justification and manager sign-off. License costs for
newly approved department-specific tools are billed back to the Finance cost
center. This list is reviewed quarterly by IT Asset Management in
coordination with Finance leadership.

title: New Hire Hardware Kit — Finance
text:
Standard hardware issued to new Finance employees includes a laptop matching the
current corporate refresh cycle, a docking station for office-based roles, a
standard monitor, keyboard, and mouse. Field or client-facing Finance roles may
additionally receive a mobile hotspot device, subject to manager approval.
Requests for non-standard hardware configurations must go through the IT
exception process with department head approval. Hardware kits are typically
prepared within three business days of a confirmed start date being logged
in the HR system.

title: Software Renewal Notice — Finance
text:
This is a standing reference document for the Finance department's annual
software license renewal cycle. License renewals for Finance-specific tools are
processed each fiscal year based on active seat counts as of the renewal
date. Department leads should review seat utilization reports sent by IT
Asset Management 60 days before renewal to identify unused seats that can be
reclaimed. Questions about specific renewal timing should be directed to IT
Asset Management, not the general IT Service Desk.

title: Guest Wi-Fi Access Policy — Chennai
text:
Guest Wi-Fi access at the Chennai office is available to visitors, vendors, and
contractors without a corporate account. Guest network credentials are
available at the Chennai front desk / reception and are valid for 24 hours.
Guest network traffic is isolated from the corporate network and does not
have access to internal file shares, applications, or printers. Employees
should not connect their own personal devices to the guest network if BYOD
enrollment is available instead, as BYOD-enrolled devices receive better
performance and access to approved internal resources.

title: VPN Access Request Procedure — Chennai
text:
Employees based at the Chennai office requiring VPN access for remote work
should submit a request through the IT Service Portal, selecting 'Chennai' as
the home office location. Approval is typically automatic for full-time
employees and requires manager approval for contractors. VPN access is
provisioned within one business day of request submission. For VPN
connectivity issues after provisioning, refer to the relevant VPN
troubleshooting knowledge base articles rather than this procedural
document.

title: Local IT Support Contact — Chennai
text:
For in-person IT support at the Chennai office, employees can visit the local IT
help desk during standard business hours. For issues outside these hours, or
for employees working remotely from the Chennai region, please log a ticket
through the central IT Service Portal or contact the 24/7 IT Service Desk
hotline. On-site hardware swaps and physical repairs are handled exclusively
by the local Chennai IT team and cannot be scheduled through the central service
desk directly.

text:

based on their seating location as recorded in the facilities system.
Requests to change a default printer assignment should be submitted through
the facilities request system, not the IT Service Desk, unless the request

title: Acceptable Use Policy for Corporate Devices
header_path: Acceptable Use Policy for Corporate Devices
text: This policy outlines acceptable use of corporate-issued devices, including laptops, mobile phones, and tablets. Devices must not be used for illegal activity, and personal use should be reasonable and not interfere with job duties. Employees are responsible for reporting lost or stolen devices immediately to IT Security. Devices remain company property and may be remotely wiped if lost, stolen, or upon employee departure.

title: Password Policy and Best Practices
text: Corporate passwords must be a minimum of 14 characters and should not reuse passwords from personal accounts. Multi-factor authentication is mandatory for all systems handling sensitive data. Passwords should be changed immediately if there is any suspicion of compromise. Password managers approved by IT Security are recommended over memorized or written-down passwords.

title: Data Classification Guidelines
text: All company data falls into one of four classification tiers: Public, Internal, Confidential, and Restricted. Restricted data (e.g., financial records, PII, PHI) requires encryption at rest and in transit, and access must be logged and reviewed quarterly. Employees handling Confidential or Restricted data should complete the annual data handling training.

title: Security Awareness Training: Phishing Overview
text: This training module covers common phishing tactics including urgency-based framing, spoofed sender addresses, and malicious attachments. Employees completing this training will learn to identify suspicious emails and understand the correct reporting process. Training completion is tracked and reported to department managers quarterly.

title: BYOD Program Overview and Eligibility
text: The Bring Your Own Device program allows eligible employees to use personal devices for work purposes after enrolling in the corporate MDM platform. Eligible device types and OS versions are listed in the program handbook. Enrollment requires acceptance of the BYOD terms, including consent to remote wipe of corporate data (not personal data) upon departure.

title: Software Request and Approval Process
text: Requests for software not on the department's pre-approved list must be submitted through the Software Request form, including business justification, estimated cost, and manager approval. Requests are reviewed by IT Asset Management within five business days. High-cost or security-sensitive requests may require additional review by IT Security.

title: IT Asset Return Process for Departing Employees
header_path: IT Asset Return Process for Departing Employees
text: Departing employees must return all IT assets (laptop, monitor, peripherals, access badges) on or before their last working day. Managers are responsible for coordinating asset return with the local IT team. Assets not returned within 10 business days of departure may result in a charge to the department's cost center.

title: Meeting Room AV Equipment Guide
text: Conference rooms are equipped with standard AV setups including a display, video conferencing camera, and wireless presentation capability. For AV issues during a meeting, use the in-room quick-start guide or contact the front desk for immediate assistance. Persistent AV equipment issues should be logged as a facilities ticket.

title: Corporate Travel IT Checklist
text: Employees traveling for business should ensure their VPN client is up to date and test connectivity before departure. International travelers should check with IT Security regarding any country-specific device restrictions. Loaner devices are available for high-risk destinations upon request through the Travel Security process.

title: Video Conferencing Etiquette Guide
text: This guide covers best practices for video meetings, including muting when not speaking, using virtual backgrounds where appropriate, and testing audio/video before important calls. Technical issues during a call should be reported after the meeting via the standard IT ticketing process.

title: IT Service Desk Hours and Contact Information
header_path: IT Service Desk Hours and Contact Information
text: The IT Service Desk is available Monday through Friday during standard business hours across all regional offices, with a 24/7 hotline for critical outages. Non-urgent requests should be submitted through the self-service portal rather than the phone line to ensure proper ticket tracking.

title: Vendor Software License Overview
text: This document summarizes the company's major enterprise software vendor relationships and license types. Individual license assignment and renewal processes are managed by IT Asset Management. Questions about specific vendor contract terms should be directed to Procurement, not the IT Service Desk.

title: Data Backup and Recovery Policy
text: Corporate file shares and databases are backed up nightly with a 30-day retention window. Employees are responsible for storing work files in approved cloud storage or shared drives rather than local-only storage, since local-only files are not covered by the corporate backup policy.

title: Mobile Device Management Enrollment Guide
text: This guide walks through enrolling a corporate or BYOD-eligible personal device into the MDM platform. Enrollment typically takes under 15 minutes and requires the employee's corporate credentials. Enrolled devices receive automatic security policy updates and can be remotely located or wiped if lost.

title: IT Change Management Process Overview
text: All changes to production systems, including software deployments and infrastructure changes, must go through the Change Advisory Board review process. Emergency changes may bypass standard review with post-hoc documentation required within 24 hours. This process does not apply to individual user-level support tickets.

title: Disaster Recovery Communication Plan
text: In the event of a major IT outage or disaster, this plan outlines communication responsibilities across IT leadership, department heads, and the broader employee base. Status updates during an active incident are posted to the company status page and the #it-incidents channel.

title: New Laptop Setup Guide
text: This self-service guide walks new employees through initial laptop setup, including connecting to Wi-Fi, signing into the corporate account, and installing standard applications from the self-service software catalog. For setup issues beyond this guide's scope, contact the IT Service Desk.

title: Email Distribution List Request Process
text: New distribution lists can be requested through the IT Service Portal. Requests must include a list owner, intended membership criteria, and business justification. Distribution lists are reviewed annually and inactive lists may be archived.

title: Shared Drive Access Request Process
text: Access to departmental shared drives is granted through group-based permissions tied to the requester's role. New access requests require approval from the drive's designated owner. This process does not cover individual file-level permission changes, which are the responsibility of the drive owner directly.

title: IT Training Calendar Overview
text: This calendar lists upcoming IT-led training sessions, including new software rollouts, security awareness refreshers, and optional productivity tool workshops. Session recordings are archived on the internal training portal for employees unable to attend live.

title: Software License Compliance Policy
text: Employees must not install unlicensed or personally-purchased software on corporate devices without going through the Software Request process. Periodic software audits are conducted to ensure license compliance across the organization. Non-compliant software found during an audit will be removed.

title: Conference Room Booking System Guide
text: Conference rooms across all offices can be booked through the corporate calendar system. Rooms equipped with specialized AV setups are marked accordingly in the booking system. No-show bookings are automatically released after 10 minutes to free up the room for walk-in use.

title: Employee Exit IT Checklist
text: This checklist for managers covers the IT-related steps required when an employee departs, including access revocation timing, asset return coordination, and email/data retention handling per company policy. Access is typically revoked at end-of-day on the employee's last working day unless otherwise specified by HR.

title: Cloud Storage Usage Guidelines
text: Employees should use only IT-approved cloud storage platforms for company data. Personal cloud storage accounts (personal Google Drive, Dropbox,     etc.) must not be used to store or share company data of any classification level, including Public-tier data, to maintain consistent audit trails.

title: IT Helpdesk SLA Overview
text: This document outlines target response and resolution times by ticket priority level. Critical incidents affecting multiple users target a response within 30 minutes. Standard individual requests target a response within one business day. SLA performance is reported monthly to IT leadership.

title: Remote Work IT Equipment Policy
text: Employees approved for remote work may request standard home-office IT equipment, including a monitor and ergonomic peripherals, subject to manager approval and budget availability. Equipment remains company property and must be returned upon request or employee departure.

title: Multi-Factor Authentication Enrollment Guide
text: This guide covers enrolling in multi-factor authentication using the corporate authenticator app. Employees should enroll a backup method (e.g., a secondary device) in case their primary authenticator is unavailable. Enrollment is mandatory within the first week of employment.

title: Internal Wiki Contribution Guidelines
text: This document covers formatting standards and review requirements for contributing to the internal knowledge wiki. All technical procedure articles should be reviewed by a subject matter expert before publishing. Outdated articles should be flagged for review rather than deleted outright, to preserve historical context.

title: Company Holiday IT Support Schedule
text: IT Service Desk coverage during company holidays is reduced to critical incident support only. Non-urgent tickets submitted during this period will be addressed on the next standard business day. The on-call rotation schedule for holiday coverage is published separately each quarter.

title: Standard Laptop Refresh Cycle Policy
text: Corporate laptops are refreshed on a standard cycle based on device age and performance benchmarks. Employees will be notified approximately 30 days before their scheduled refresh. Requests for an early refresh outside the standard cycle require manager approval and a documented business justification.

title: IT Procurement Request Process
text: Hardware and software procurement requests above standard issued equipment must go through the IT Procurement process, including budget approval from the requesting department. Standard turnaround time is 10 business days from budget approval to fulfillment.

title: Internal Tool Access Matrix Overview
text: This reference document summarizes which internal tools are accessible by default to each department, and which require an additional access request. It is intended as a planning reference for managers, not as a self-service access request mechanism.
